doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Goals: what it means to make it
summary: Discussing the opening of his book, Ricker says goals shift over a career; he once hoped to teach high school band in Denver.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I like the way you started your book, Lessons from a Street-Wise Professor with this bit about goals. And I remember being at Fredonia and the jazz guys were sort of their own club. And we all wanted to make it. And I remember that phrase but I don’t remember being really aware of what that meant to us. We just wanted to make it. And you addressed that. Can you speak about that a little bit?
Jeez I can’t remember what I said about it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
Well it was like what means the most to you? Making a lot of money? Working with underprivileged kids?

Sure. What is the big deal for you. Well in my own case I’ll just say that when I started off in college, I wanted to be a, I thought if I could teach a high school band in Denver that’d be the greatest thing in the world. And that’s what I thought of doing. But it’s along the way I met people and, you know, and one thing led to another. Another opportunity came up. But I think the thing, Monk, that you’re referring to is that if you think you want to be, okay when you’re first out of school playing on a cruise ship might be good. Okay? It might be fun. But you know when you’re 55 years old or so and you’re looking like oh wow man, I may retire in a while, it’s not that cool. And so the — I think you know that you kind of move the goal post as you get, as you grow up and learn more and get more experience, and, you know, kind of adjust the rudder to make sure you’re still moving ahead. I think the goal should be whatever really makes you happy. It could be finding a mate. You know? Hopefully that’ll happen as well as finding a good job. You know? I’m sorry I’m not really zeroing in on it very well.
